module MyGem
  # Rails 7.2+ removed the class-level ActiveSupport::Deprecation.warn API,
  # so a deprecator instance is created and used instead.
  DEPRECATOR = ActiveSupport::Deprecation.new("1.0", "MyGem")

  def self.old_api
    DEPRECATOR.warn("old_api is deprecated")
    42
  end
end

module MyGem
  # Instance-based deprecator (the ActiveSupport::Deprecation singleton API
  # is no longer supported in current Rails releases).
  DEPRECATOR = ActiveSupport::Deprecation.new("1.0", "MyGem")

  def self.old_api
    DEPRECATOR.warn("old_api is deprecated")
    42
  end
end

module ReportFormatter
  # Uses Rails' built-in Time::DATE_FORMATS[:db] ("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S").
  # Example: "2026-01-02 03:04:05"
  def self.stamp(time)
    time.to_fs(:db)
  end

  # Uses Rails' built-in Date::DATE_FORMATS[:long] ("%B %d, %Y").
  # Example: "January 02, 2026"
  def self.long_date(date)
    date.to_fs(:long)
  end
end

module ReportFormatter
  # Formats a time using Rails' built-in :db format (e.g. "2026-01-02 03:04:05").
  def self.stamp(time)
    time.to_fs(:db)
  end

  # Formats a date using Rails' built-in :long format (e.g. "January 02, 2026").
  def self.long_date(date)
    date.to_fs(:long)
  end
end

# Targets Rails 8.x (latest stable). Assumes ActiveSupport core extensions are loaded.
#
# Time::DATE_FORMATS[:db]  => "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"  (e.g. "2026-01-02 03:04:05")
# Date::DATE_FORMATS[:long] => "%B %d, %Y"          (e.g. "January 02, 2026")

module ReportFormatter
  # Formats a time using Rails' built-in :db format.
  def self.stamp(time)
    time.to_fs(:db)
  end

  # Formats a date using Rails' built-in :long format.
  def self.long_date(date)
    date.to_fs(:long)
  end
end

class UsersController < ActionController::API
  def create
    # A plain string (or array) in place of the nested user object is a client error.
    unless params[:user].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
      render json: { error: "user must be a nested object" }, status: :bad_request
      return
    end

    # Only :name is permitted; any other keys under user are silently dropped.
    user_params = params.require(:user).permit(:name)

    render json: user_params.to_h, status: :ok
  end
end

class UsersController < ActionController::API
  rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing, with: :bad_request

  def create
    user_params = params.require(:user)
    return bad_request unless user_params.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

    render json: user_params.permit(:name).to_h, status: :ok
  end

  private

  def bad_request
    render json: { error: "Bad Request" }, status: :bad_request
  end
end

class UsersController < ActionController::API
  def create
    # A plain string (or missing key) under "user" is a malformed request.
    unless params[:user].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
      render json: { error: "param 'user' must be a nested object" }, status: :bad_request
      return
    end

    # Only user[name] is permitted; any other keys are dropped.
    permitted = params.require(:user).permit(:name)

    render json: permitted.to_h, status: :ok
  end
end
